newsitem.title: POLAND: DHL sees Polish sales up 40 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: DHL sees Polish sales up 40 pct in 1997.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express expects to increase its sales in Poland to 70 million zlotys this year from 50 million zlotys in 1996, the president of the company's Polish unit told a news conference on Monady.
Alan Cassels said DHL's sales in Poland rose 53 percent in 1996 against 1995.

"Our next goal (in Poland) is to open an air connection from Poland to Copenhagen," Cassels said adding the firm already operated a Boeing 727 from Warsaw to Brussels via Berlin and an Antonov-26 from Katowice to Berlin.
The company, employing 480, has 21 bureaus in Poland and uses 160 cars to handle more than 4,000 parcels a day.
Cassels estimates that DHL has about 60 percent share of international parcel deliveries in Poland.
